title: Years in the Army and discharge
summary: Clarifying Cornbread dates; he entered in February 1942, left in 1946 disgusted with promotions, in Army ammunition ordnance.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh, about cornbread, too. You were 16, you said?
No, I was only 16 when I left, played with cornbread about 8 and J.

Yeah, I mean, after I come out, I played with cornbread at the age of 16, but after that, I must have been in my, way in my 20s, after I come out of the service, and I played with my 8 and J. Truthfully, I did the play with him by 8 and J. after I come out, when I came out, I'd come out of the service on the furlough, and he was playing 8 and J ball in 1943 or 44, on my first furlough I was going to play with. And I did a few years, a couple of years and some months, I'd come back, I played with him again there.
What year did you get out of the service? What day?
I got out of the service in 46.

Oh yeah, well, see, I was going to make, I was getting ready, I was going to make a career in the service. So I went in the service, early 40, like, early 40, I went in 42 February, and I stood the 46th. I re-up and everything, you know. I made a nice little rating in the service, and then after they had people, after the war was over, they had people coming in the service, wouldn't have no one push around, and they didn't know anything, you know.

So that made me disgusted. So if they had a little 90 dead wonder, you know. We went to school for 90 dead and get a little brass ball on their shoulder, you know. And I knew much about what I was doing, and they didn't knew, and they had to ask me, but they still wanted to dog me around. So I didn't dispute the custody, I just went on it. But during that time, you know, if you resigned and all that kind of stuff, you know, you got points where you could get out, they don't hold you. So I just, you know, told them I'd come to command, I'd like to get on out to the service. Told them I was ready.
What branch of the service were you in?
I was in the ammunition. Ordnance. Army or? Ordnance. Army or?
Army, yeah. Army ammunition. Oh, I see. Army ammunition. Oh, who was in Bunk's band?
I forgot to ask you that. Do you remember? Yeah, well that would be easy to remember. What was the first job you played? My first job I played? Oh, man, that's really a fact.
